claims.text: The baseline is an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy.
The baseline has a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state.
Combined high-pressure and high-temperature treatment can convert an Mg-containing lightweight alloy into a single-phase solid solution.
Formation of the single-phase solid solution can overcome limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation.
The treatment temperature should be above 600 K.
High pressure is required for the treatment.
The exposure should continue long enough to form a single-phase solid solution.
High pressure decreases atomic-size differences between the solute elements and the alloy matrix.
High pressure decreases electronegativity differences between the solute elements and the alloy matrix.
A synergistic high-entropy effect under combined high temperature and high pressure promotes formation of the single-phase alloy.
The treatment will improve room-temperature compressive behavior relative to the as-processed baseline.
The treatment will improve corrosion resistance relative to the as-processed baseline.
The treatment will improve resistance to high-temperature oxidation relative to the as-processed baseline.
The hypothesis is bounded to temperatures below 700 °C.
The relevant test environments are inert or chloride-containing environments.

contradictions.description: High-temperature oxidation resistance is a predicted and measured outcome, but the stated environments are inert or chloride-containing; no oxidizing atmosphere is defined, so the oxidation outcome cannot be tested within the stated boundary.
